name: Fertiliser supply
summary: Egyptian urea near $535 a tonne after gas cuts to plants; US retail urea 11% above a year earlier
state: Egyptian producer Kima said its gas supply was cut by 20% from 1 Nov, and Egyptian granular urea for November is about $535 a tonne FOB, up about 17% from September (Fertilizer Daily, 9 Nov). US retail urea averaged $662 a ton in the week to 6 Nov, down 1.5% on the month but 11% above a year earlier (DTN, 11 Nov). Gulf exports remain disrupted by the Hormuz restrictions, but no 60% three-month rise or fully closed route was found as of 13 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Farmers buying nitrogen fertiliser for spring face higher costs than a year ago, which tends to feed into crop planting decisions and, later, food prices.
rubric_hit: Gulf export route disrupted and Egyptian gas cuts (Watch); urea +17% since Sep < 60% Alert line

sources.title: Fertilizer Daily — Egyptian urea price rises amid gas cuts
DTN — Retail Fertilizer Prices Mixed During First Week of November

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
